title: Reading documents
passage:
Planning note | Market Voices evening
At our evening of market recordings, we will play three short clips made by people who worked around the square. The history society usually comes as a group. Its members know many of the speakers’ names, but some have never been to the market. The stallholders’ Thursday supper group knows the square well; most of them started working here after the recordings were made.

One person will host each clip. They can use a short lead-in and invite a response afterward. The large yellow side door is the public entrance; the door facing the square is for performers. Once playback begins, the yellow door can be opened from inside only, to keep street noise out. The welcome volunteer can admit or readmit listeners through the glass lobby door if they ring its bell. The bell at the square door is for performers.

During the first clip last time, a late arrival had to step past three people to reach the only empty chair. This time, leave the two seats nearest the aisle in the back row empty at the start. At the first break, anyone can take an empty seat there.

When we prepare recordings, we can reduce isolated noise that hides a speaker. A pause that demonstrates what the speaker is describing belongs in the story, even when the recording was made later. The recording notes use a filled dot for a cue sent to the speaker; an open dot is a cue the speaker sent to the person at the controls. In this session a cue sent to Bert meant wait for a level check. The cue in the other direction meant Bert was ready for the sound he had requested. If a pause is just for an equipment check, tighten it without cutting anything the speaker says.

The keeper of the parcel counter lent us a photograph of the chalkboard. A helper wrote names on it in the order people reached the counter. Each name stayed in that sequence until it was called. It was not a list of purchases, and writing a name did not mean a parcel was ready.

Clara’s note to the three clip hosts
Hello, everyone. I asked Nina why she said she didn’t want to feel ‘like a visitor in our own market.’ She told me about Thursday supper: ‘We all knew exactly where the old bread stall was. Then someone mentioned Bert, and Jo asked if that was the man from the council.’

Vera wondered if we should invite the supper group to tell their stories first, while people are still settling in. Imran thought we could just introduce each speaker and go straight to the next clip when it ends. Vera did find one helpful line for the introduction: ‘Bert used to mend market umbrellas in the stall behind the bakery.’

For whoever edits Bert’s recording: he talks about two calls at the market. In both accounts, he mentions that the vendors had to stop talking to listen, and then his voice drops out. There’s a gap marked with a filled dot in the first account; the gap in the second account is marked with an open dot. We hear the same bell clip at the end of both gaps. Both gaps fall between complete phrases. Please send me the edited clip to check.

One more detail for the last host. In Marta’s recording we go from the clock tower to the steps outside the old market office. We’re on those steps when she sings a line and says, ‘We always sang it here.’ I asked if the song helped people find the market. She laughed and said, ‘They’d found it by then. That was how we told them we were done for the day.’ Nina also said she may step out through the yellow door to take a call after we start playing the first clip. She expects to be able to come back in without waiting for a break.

After that discussion, Nina sent another message about the last recording evening. ‘Jo had a story ready, but when the host called on our table, the whole room turned to look at him. He didn’t say a word. On the walk home, he told the person next to him the entire story.’

One more thought for Marta’s clip. She laughed when the interviewer asked why her brother was buying eggs while she waited for their parcel. ‘He wasn’t jumping the queue. I told him the chalk could do the waiting for him.’ They came back together when the helper called his name. The interviewer’s draft says the helper used the board to get parcels ready sooner. Before we use that introduction, explain what staying on the board let him do. Thanks, Clara
passageZh:
籌備便條｜市場之聲分享會
市場錄音分享會上，我們會播放三段短錄音，由曾在廣場周邊工作的人錄製。地方歷史協會通常會團體出席。會員知道許多錄音者的名字，但有些人從沒來過這座市場。攤商的週四聚餐小組很熟悉廣場；他們多半是在錄音完成後才來這裡工作。

每段錄音都有一位主持人，可以先做簡短引介，播完再邀請聽眾回應。黃色大側門是民眾入口，面向廣場的門供演出人員使用。錄音開始播放後，黃色側門只能從裡面打開，以免街上的聲音傳進來。聽眾按門廳玻璃門旁的門鈴，接待志工就能讓他們入場或回場。廣場門的門鈴供演出人員使用。

上次播放第一段錄音時，有人遲到，得從三個人面前擠過去才能坐到唯一的空位。這次開始時，請把最後一排最靠走道的兩個座位先空下來。第一次休息時，這兩席如果還空著，任何人都可以坐。

整理錄音時，如果某個突發噪音蓋過說話聲，可以把音量調低。如果停頓是說話者在示範故事裡的情況，即使錄音是事後才錄的，仍屬於故事的一部分。錄音紀錄用實心點標示傳給說話者的訊號，空心點則是說話者傳給控台人員的訊號。這次傳給伯特的訊號是請他等待音量檢查；反方向的訊號則表示伯特已準備好，請對方播放他要求的聲音。如果停頓只是為了檢查設備，可以縮短，但不要剪掉說話者的任何話。

包裹櫃臺的管理員借給我們一張黑板的照片。助手按照人們到達櫃臺的先後，把名字寫在上面。輪到叫某個名字之前，那個名字會留在原本的順序裡。那不是購物清單，寫上名字也不表示包裹已準備好。

克拉拉寫給三位錄音主持人的信
各位好。我問妮娜，為什麼她說不想「在自己的市場裡像個外來的訪客」。她提到週四聚餐時的情形：「我們都很清楚以前的麵包攤在哪裡。後來有人提起伯特，喬就問，是不是市議會的那個人。」

薇拉在想，要不要請聚餐小組在大家還在入座時先說自己的故事。伊姆蘭認為，我們可以介紹錄音中的人，每段播完就直接播下一段。薇拉確實找到一句可以用在開場的話：「伯特以前在麵包坊後面的攤位修市場的遮陽傘。」

給剪輯伯特錄音的人：他談到市場上的兩種信號。兩段敘述裡，他都提到攤商得先停止交談才能聽見，接著就不再說話。第一段的停頓標了實心點，第二段的停頓標了空心點。兩段停頓結尾都聽得到同一段鈴聲錄音，兩段停頓都在完整語句之間。請把剪好的錄音傳給我確認。

最後一位主持人還有個細節要注意。瑪塔的錄音裡，我們先到鐘塔，後來走到舊市場辦公室外的階梯。她唱了一句，說「我們以前都在這裡唱」時，我們就站在那些階梯上。我問，那首歌是不是為了讓大家找到市場。她笑著說：「那時候他們早就找到啦。那是我們跟大家說今天收攤了的方式。」妮娜也說，第一段錄音開始播放後，她可能會從黃色側門出去接電話。她希望不用等到休息時間就能回場。

討論完後，妮娜又傳來一則訊息，說起上次的錄音分享會：「喬都準備好要說一段故事了，可是主持人點到我們這桌時，整個房間的人都轉過來看他，他一句話也沒說。走路回家時，他把整段故事都說給旁邊的人聽了。」

關於瑪塔的錄音，還有一點。訪談者問她，為什麼她等包裹時，哥哥卻跑去買蛋。她笑著說：「他可沒有插隊。我跟他說，讓粉筆替他等就好。」助手叫到哥哥的名字時，兩人一起回到櫃臺。訪談者的開場稿說，助手用黑板加快準備包裹的速度。在採用那段開場前，請先說明名字留在黑板上，讓她哥哥可以做什麼。謝謝，克拉拉
